I now have a clear picture. Here's the diagnosis:

---

## Build Performance Diagnosis — Contoso.WebApi

**Project:** 1 source file, 45 lines | **Build time:** ~1.7s (successful) — excessive for this size.

### 🔍 Root Cause: Analyzer Overload

This tiny project loads **5 overlapping analyzer packages**:

| Source | Package | Scope |
|--------|---------|-------|
| `.csproj` | Roslynator.Analyzers | 500+ rules |
| `.csproj` | SonarAnalyzer.CSharp | 400+ rules |
| `.csproj` | Meziantou.Analyzer | 300+ rules |
| `Directory.Build.props` | Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers | 200+ rules (GlobalPackageReference) |
| `Directory.Build.props` | StyleCop.Analyzers | 200+ rules (GlobalPackageReference) |

Plus `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true` enables **IDE code-style analyzers** in the build, adding yet another analyzer pass.

These analyzers have **massive rule overlap** (naming, style, quality) — they're competing to flag the same issues (evidenced by both `MA0002` and `CA1305` firing on the same patterns).

### 📊 Time Breakdown (1.7s total)

| Task | Time | % |
|------|------|---|
| NuGet Restore | 543ms | 32% |
| MSBuild orchestration | 178ms | 10% |
| **Csc (compile + analyzers)** | **115ms** | **7%** |
| ResolvePackageAssets | 58ms | 3% |
| ProcessFrameworkReferences | 55ms | 3% |

### ✅ Recommended Fixes (Priority Order)

**1. Consolidate analyzers — pick ONE third-party analyzer**

The biggest win. Choose **one** of Roslynator, SonarAnalyzer, or Meziantou — not all three. The built-in `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers` (included in the SDK for .NET 8+) already covers CA rules. Recommendation:

```xml
<!-- Keep the SDK's built-in NetAnalyzers (already in .NET 8 SDK) -->
<!-- Remove the explicit GlobalPackageReference for NetAnalyzers v8.0.0 — it's redundant -->

<!-- Pick ONE third-party analyzer, e.g. Meziantou: -->
<PackageReference Include="Meziantou.Analyzer" Version="2.0.127" />

<!-- REMOVE these: -->
<!-- <PackageReference Include="Roslynator.Analyzers" ... /> -->
<!-- <PackageReference Include="SonarAnalyzer.CSharp" ... /> -->
```

**2. Remove redundant `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers` GlobalPackageReference**

.NET 8 SDK already bundles NetAnalyzers. The explicit `GlobalPackageReference` for v8.0.0 is redundant and adds restore/resolution overhead.

**3. Reconsider `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild`**

This adds IDE style analyzers (IDE0008, IDE0011, IDE0028, IDE0046, IDE0160, IDE0290) to every CLI build. These are better enforced in the IDE or CI only:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props, limit to CI: -->
<EnforceCodeStyleInBuild Condition="'$(CI)' == 'true'">true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
```

**4. Evaluate `GenerateDocumentationFile`**

This triggers CS1591 for every public member without XML docs (6 warnings here). If this is an internal service, disable it:

```xml
<GenerateDocumentationFile>false</GenerateDocumentationFile>
```

**5. Use `StyleCop.Analyzers` OR `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` — not both**

StyleCop and IDE code-style analyzers overlap significantly on formatting/naming rules. Pick one approach.

### Impact Estimate

Consolidating to 1-2 analyzer packages and removing `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` from local builds will reduce per-project analyzer overhead by ~60-70%, and the benefit scales linearly as you add more projects/files to the solution.
